results.title: Official WoW Classic Hardcore rules explained: Deaths, PvP, dungeons, and more
excerpts:
The feature had been popularized by the _WoW_ community at large, with players and streamers taking part in Hardcore _WoW_ runs dating back to last year. The game mode surged in popularity earlier this year, with add-ons, community rules, and forums all popping up to drive the Hardcore _Classic WoW_ experience even further.

Now, Blizzard Entertainment is streamlining the experience. Official Hardcore servers are launching in just a few weeks, and many of the same rules that allowed the game mode to become a smash hit within the community are staying intact. The famous “permadeath” rule is obviously transferring over, while other quality-of-life changes are also being introduced to make Hardcore _WoW_ even more applicable to a broader audience.

Here’s **everything you need to know about official Hardcore _Classic WoW_ servers** , including all of the rule changes and updates coming to the game mode when it launches.

## _WoW Classic_ Hardcore’s biggest rule: Permadeath
**The driving principle of _WoW Classic_ Hardcore is its permanent death rule** . When your character dies, it dies for good—no negotiating, no second chances. Upon death, you lose all progress you made with your character, and you have to head back to the character select screen and start your journey all over again.

This concept has been present in _WoW Classic_ Hardcore runs ever since the game mode was popularized within the community. While it sounds brutal and unforgiving, the satisfaction you get from going as far as reaching full level 60, for example, is unmatched.

Now that Hardcore servers are official, the permadeath rule is sticking around as the mode’s most important pillar. Regardless of whether you’re level 20 or level 60, your character is gone forever after they suffer their first death.

## Dungeon timers and lockouts explained in _WoW Classic_ Hardcore

A screenshot of the Scarlet Monastery in WoW Classic, exterior.

...

## Is PvP enabled on _Classic_ Hardcore servers?

Classic WoW Stranglethrorn Vale Paladin, who runs forward in a rainy forest, chased by an orc, with bright light glowing from both hands PvP is a trademark part of WoW Classic’s gameplay. Image via Blizzard Entertainment

**PvP is enabled on an opt-in basis in _WoW Classic_ Hardcore** . There’s no need to worry about being attacked by another player against your will and having to engage them in combat to save your life. If you’re brave and confident, you can enable PvP, by typing “/pvp” in chat to flag yourself for combat.

**Related: The best and the worst classes for _WoW Hardcore_**

A new feature that’s being introduced to official Hardcore servers called “Duel to the Death” will allow players to engage each other in one-on-one combat. Players who win consecutive duels will get a stacking buff attached to their character that shows off how many battles they’ve won against other players.
Furthermore, Battlegrounds are not enabled on Hardcore realms, but Wargames are. The rules of permanent death are still enabled in Wargames, though, despite the lack of rewards that will come from PvP in Hardcore _Classic WoW_ .

## What happens if your character dies in _WoW Classic_ Hardcore?

Should your _Wow Classic_ Hardcore character die in the midst of their leveling journey, you’ll be able to temporarily access your character as a ghost and take care of any loose ends that may have been left open after your death (such as player-to-player communication and the transferring of any ranks within your guild). **You’ll also have the option to transfer your Hardcore character to a non-Hardcore server after your death and continue your progression normally** . But, as mentioned previously, you will not be able to continue making progress with your character on Hardcore servers.

## Other rules and regulations coming to Hardcore _Classic WoW_

Last updated on Jul 02, 2023 at 12:00 by Sellin [3 comments](https://www.icy-veins.com/forums/topic/73595-hardcore-servers)

This guide covers everything you need to know about the new rules/changes implemented into

## Hardcore Rules

Blizzard is releasing Hardcore Classic World of Warcraft server, and with this new
game mode comes a unique set of rules that will greatly impact your experience while playing.
Most of these rules are structured in a way to make the perma-death rule set more fair,
eliminating outside interference so the game feels more fair. The original Classic game
was not designed with the Hardcore rule set in mind.

1\.1.

### Death is Permanent

If your character dies on Hardcore, you will not be able to revive, but are
still able to operate inside of the game world as a Ghost. This is largely to
be able to communicate with other players and handle various administrative tasks.
This applies to stuff such as handing off Guild Leader to another character.
Blizzard has offered free server transfers from the Hardcore servers to the
Forever Classic servers if your character dies on Hardcore. Essentially this
means your character is not gone forever, it just becomes unplayable on Hardcore.

2\.

## PvP Changes

The largest change to PvP in Hardcore Classic is the removal of the ability to
queue for battlegrounds. You may still engage in pre-made Wargames against other groups,

# Official Hardcore Rules Explained

Passion [Passion](https://www.warcrafttavern.com/participant/passion/) • Published June 28, 2023

Today we have received our first official clarification on the rules of the official Classic Era Hardcore servers that are releasing soon™.

Beginning with the obvious one, death is permanent. On Hardcore realms you will be able to release your spirit and play as a ghost, but you will not be able to revive through any means. This means you cannot use either Soulstones or Reincarnation for a second wind. While unconfirmed, this likely also includes [Twisting Nether](https://wowclassicdb.com/item/19290) . Dead characters will not be permanently stuck as a ghost, and will be able to utilize free server transfers to move over to a non-Hardcore realm instead.

The removal of the buff and debuff limit that was present on Season of Mastery will also be present here, allowing groups to surpass the 16 debuff limit of standard Classic Era.
In another carry-over from Season of Mastery, dungeon groups will give significantly reduced experience if anyone in the party is much higher level. This was initially implemented to devalue boosting for experience, and will likely serve the same function on Hardcore realms. This does not prohibit you from being boosted exclusively to get better gear with minimal risk to yourself, although a level 60 player cannot do dungeons with anyone below level 60.

Additionally, dungeons will have a minimum of a 24-hour lockout timer. This means that players cannot do the same dungeon more than once in a 24-hour period. This may be seen as a bit of a light change compared to the Hardcore addon, which restricts players from doing any dungeon more than once. This change seems to be a mostly reasonable middle-ground, allowing players to enjoy the “MMO” part of this MMORPG a bit more.

...

This feature will allow players to either right click a portrait and select it, or type /makgora to challenge a player. Losing one of these duels will count as your one and only death for that character. Winning will grant you a stack of “String of Ears”, effectively a trophy displaying how many players you have killed.

Finally, Hardcore realms will not function as a new Season, and will have all content available from day 1, including the overhauled dungeon loot, and all raids.

If you want to try Hardcore realms early, you can join the Public Test Realms starting June 29th. These realms will go up to level 30 for the time being. Remember, Hardcore is all about trying again and again, so losing your PTR progress when the servers release is just more practice.

The full article can be found below.

## References

Blizzard Entertainment [Source](https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-gb/news/23973734/rules-of-engagement-classic-hardcore-is-coming-to-world-of-warcraft)

While PvP is a fun part of _World of Warcraft_ , by allowing players to enter battlegrounds on one-life characters, there is a concern that this would lead to overly defensive play, often to the point of non-participation, especially when you consider how powerful some rewards are from factions such as Stormpike Guard and the Frostwolf Clan. PvP is not the focus of the Hardcore game mode, so we’ve decided to disable normal PvP queuing entirely. If you wish to test yourself in pre-arranged Wargames, however, that’s an available option.  Wargames confer no honor or other rewards. Beware—if you engage in Wargames, death is still permanent.

#### **PvP and Quest Updates**

Various quests and objectives that cause players to become PvP flagged, such as the quest, “The Attack” and,  “The Missing Diplomat,” no longer cause players to become flagged for PvP.

...

We do recognize that there may be a desire to run a dungeon while leveling multiple times, such as to finish a quest or get an important piece of loot. As a result, we’ve added a 24-hour timer to almost all dungeons for players until they hit level 60. By extension, this also means that level 60 players may never enter lower-level dungeons with players below level 60 for any reason.

Additionally, we’ve carried over the group experience restrictions from Season of Mastery—meaning that players that are significantly higher level than the creatures in a given dungeon will cause those creatures to grant trivial experience to the other members of the group. Higher-level characters “power-leveling” lower-level characters are not something that we feel is appropriate for WoW Classic Hardcore.

#### **To Buff or Debuff**

The 16 debuff limit and 32 buff limits have been removed on Hardcore realms.

...

While Paladins have enormous tools to prevent death, a Shaman’s core tool to recover from death is wholly incompatible with Hardcore. As a result, we are removing the ability for Paladins to use their various immunity abilities to safely cast Hearthstone and escape danger.

#### **A Duel to the Death**

A new feature has been added to Hardcore realms: Duel to the Death.

To issue a Duel to the Death, you will need to right-click the target’s portrait and request a Duel to the Death from the context menu.  A Duel to the Death can also be triggered by selecting the target and typing /makgora in your chat window. Before commencing combat, both parties must read and acknowledge a warning message and type “I Agree” to begin.

As one may expect, death in a Duel to the Death is permanent, just like any other death on Hardcore realms.
We feel that this is going to be an extremely exciting addition to Hardcore realms for those who like to play at the highest possible stakes, and those who wish to spectate such contests of honor.

Since bragging rights are important, we will be tracking the number of kills you receive in Duels to the Death with a special cosmetic buff on your character called “String of Ears”. Each time you win a Duel to the Death, you will receive a “trophy,” and the stack count on this buff will increase by 1. Anyone who clicks on your character will be able to see what a frightful combatant you are by the number of Ears you’ve collected. There are some limitations to this, however, as you cannot earn the String of Ears buff before level 10, and you cannot earn the buff if you and your opponent are too many levels apart.

## Description

# Hardcore Mode
Brings the official Hardcore realm experience to any non-hardcore realm — complete with permanent death, rulesets, leaderboards, and announcements for everyone to see.

## Features

* **Ruleset System** : Fresh characters (level 1, no XP or money earned) can choose a ruleset upon entering the world. Non-fresh characters can also enable the addon, provided they have the Soul of Iron buff to prove they never died, but are locked to **Normal** . All restrictions are actively enforced, and blocked actions send an automatic whisper to the other player explaining why.
  
    + **Normal** : No restrictions; trading, the Auction House, mail, and grouping are all allowed.
    + **Self-Found** : Trading, the Auction House, and mailing items are not allowed. Items and gold must be earned on your own.
    + **Solo Self-Found** : Everything in Self-Found, plus no grouping with other players.
* **Death Tracking & Announcements** : Every death is recorded with its cause, area, date, and last words.
The addon supports two types of announcements, replicating the official Hardcore realm experience: chat messages and raid-style alerts. Both are configurable independently, and a minimum level threshold can be set to suppress announcements for deaths below a chosen level:
  
    + **Guild** : Announced only to guild members.
    + **All** : Announced to all same-faction addon users on the realm.
    + **Disabled** : No announcement.
* **Death Popup** : On death, a popup appears with the choice to "Try again!" (to log out) and "Release Spirit" (to become a ghost). Another popup replaces the standard corpse recovery and resurrection prompts — both matching the official Hardcore realm experience.
* **Players Window** : A live leaderboard of all same-faction Hardcore Mode addon users on the realm. Filterable by guild, recently seen, or free-text search, and sortable by any column.
Click any player to whisper them, Shift+click to look them up with /who, or right-click for a context menu with options to whisper, invite, copy the character name, or copy the guild name.
* **Deaths Window** : A complete record of all known same-faction deaths on the realm, including cause of death and last words. Filterable by guild or free-text search, and sortable by any column.
* **Soul of Iron Buff Tracking** : On realms where Soul of Iron is available, shows its status for you and other players — whether they have it, have lost it, or are unknown — and notifies you when it's first detected.
* **Last Words** : Your last chat message before dying is saved in the Deaths window and announced in guild chat if you're in one. You can configure which chat channels are monitored for last words.
* **Character Sheet & Tooltip Integration** : Your Hardcore status and ruleset are shown on the character sheet.
Hovering over other addon users also shows their Hardcore status in the tooltip.
* **Level Milestones** : Max level achievements are announced to all same-faction addon users on the realm. Every 10 levels, a milestone is also announced in guild chat.
* **Authentic Hardcore Sounds** : Plays sound effects matching the official Hardcore realm experience on death and max level.
* **Minimap Button** : A minimap button for quick access — left-click opens the Players window, right-click opens the Deaths window, Shift+right-click opens Options, and Ctrl+right-click toggles the button's visibility.
* **Options & Configuration** : Configure death announcement scope, death alerts, minimum level threshold for announcements, last words channels, player online/offline alerts, minimap visibility, whisper suppression, and more. Supports AceDB profiles with settings that can be scoped per character, realm, class, race, faction, locale, or shared globally.

## Limitations
* **Addon required on both ends** : Players who are not running the addon are completely invisible to the Hardcore Mode network. They will not see death or max-level announcements, cannot help relay messages to others, and their own data will not appear in the Players or Deaths windows.
* **Protected actions on death** : Unlike official Hardcore realms, the addon cannot automatically log you out or transfer your guild leadership when you die — both are protected game functions that addons cannot access. Clicking "Try again!" opens the game menu instead, and guild leadership must be transferred manually.
* **Not everything can be blocked** : The addon tries its best to enforce restrictions on trading, mail, grouping, and the Auction House, but some things simply cannot be blocked — such as the use of items, spells, or abilities that would be off-limits on official Hardcore realms. The honor system applies for what falls outside the addon's reach.

## The Hardcore Mode Team
